thesis: Computations and interpreter construction are actions whose expected decision benefits must outweigh full lifetime costs.

ideas.statement: Computations and interpreter construction are actions whose expected decision benefits must outweigh full lifetime costs.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Two individually unhelpful bit observations jointly determine whether bits differ; interpreter investment of 1,000 ms amortizes after 34 uses under stated costs.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Bounded selection must be compared with simple policies, and optimizing supplied utility does not determine legitimate human objectives.

audit.notes: Source-grounded analysis; proposed mechanisms and limited guarantees preserved.
